system.name: Visual Planning
system.one_liner: A paradigm where a large vision model plans by predicting a sequence of images, trained with reinforcement learning (VPRL), instead of reasoning in text.

content.variant_note: three stacked lanes with one Input-to-output grammar: direct prompting, verbal chain-of-thought, visual thoughts; only box colour and the content under each box change
content.argues: Traditional paradigms produce verbose and inaccurate textual plans, whereas Visual Planning predicts the next visual state directly as a pure image trajectory.
content.subject: Three reasoning paradigms drawn as input-to-output chains for a map-navigation example: direct prompting, multimodal chain-of-thought and visual planning.

new_tags.name: gradient-outline-mixed-modality

lessons.what_to_learn: Compare paradigms by drawing each as the same Input-steps-Output chain on its own lane and letting colour carry the single difference (blue text boxes versus purple image boxes), with a two-swatch key in the corner and the content of each step written or pictured under its box.
lessons.suits: Paradigm comparisons where the contrast is the medium of the intermediate steps (text versus image versus code), such as chain-of-thought variants and modality-specific reasoning.

evidence: The traditional approaches (top and middle rows) generate verbose and inaccurate textual plan
the Visual Planning paradigm (bottom row) predicts the next visual state directly, forming a pure image trajectory without language mediation
planning is executed via sequences of images that encode step-by-step inference in the visual domain

summary: Visual Planning proposes planning with sequences of images instead of text. Figure 1 compares three reasoning paradigms as three stacked lanes with the same grammar: rounded boxes joined by arrows from an input to an output, outlined in blue for text and purple for image according to a key in the corner. Direct Prompting maps an image-and-text input straight to a verbal output; Multimodal Chain-of-Thought inserts verbal thought boxes with italic plan sentences under them; Visual Planning replaces them with purple Visual Thought boxes, each with a map thumbnail in which a navigation marker moves toward a pin, plus a robot with a thought cloud of tiny pictures at the input.
summary_zh: 视觉规划主张用图像序列而非文字做规划。图把三种推理范式画成同一输入到输出的三条横向泳道：直接提示、多模态思维链（蓝框文字思考）和视觉规划（紫框图像思考，地图上的导航标记逐步移动），角落图例以蓝色表示文本、紫色表示图像。
notes: Prior kinds kept; the variant is changed from design-family to paired-lanes because the three lanes redraw one chain. The lanes are titled but unframed and share one key, so the figure is counted as one drawing with lanes (panel_count 1). No body paragraph mentions the figure; roles come from the caption and the figure. The gradient-outlined Input boxes are inferred to be the two 52 x 18 pt placed bitmaps.
